authorCorrections: Updated current TLS reference to RFC 9846 (July 2026), retaining RFC 8446 as the historical original. CertificateVerify dictionary definition now includes context-bound signature input; not every TLS record is encrypted; HelloRetryRequest can request a cookie as well as a key share.
Corrected glossary forward-secrecy/ephemeral-key claims to require the negotiated authenticated mode and appropriate secret handling; PSK-only and early-data exceptions remain explicit.

Corrected public-root trust, trust-anchor handling, intermediate-certificate delivery, leaf identity scope, certificate pinning and OCSP lookup/privacy simplifications. Short validity makes renewal reliability important; it does not mathematically require automation.

Corrected WPA2 offline-verifier equality: a matching finite MIC supplies strong evidence, not a logical proof that the guess equals the passphrase. Password-search mean is explicitly approximate for the large without-replacement model.

Corrected WPA2 versus SAE passphrase/PMK scope: WPA2 passphrase provisioning uses the stated ASCII bounds, while SAE provisioning and PMK length depend on negotiated methods. WPA2/WPA3 transition mode and Transition Disable are distinct entries.

Corrected nonce/IV universal requirements to construction-specific requirements, and key reinstallation to a problem when security counters/state reset. CCMP packet number is one nonce component and uniqueness is scoped to the key and nonce context.

Distinguished rogue AP from an evil twin, BSS infrastructure from independent/ad-hoc operation, and controlled from uncontrolled 802.1X traffic paths. EAP authentication roles no longer imply every wired authenticator runs the wireless four-way handshake.

Corrected nftables base versus regular chains, first-match policy ordering, conntrack timeout configurability and IPv4-only versus inet-family behaviour. Idle tracking expiry is not universally a silent endpoint close.

Qualified tunnel-MTU behaviour at the encapsulating endpoint versus forwarding-router PMTUD. MSS clamping is a TCP mitigation, not a universal repair. Full-tunnel routing and AllowedIPs include OS route selection and endpoint exceptions.

Corrected ESP tunnel-mode confidentiality to depend on negotiated protection, AES-GCM ICV permitted lengths to 8/12/16, ESP padding assumptions, and underlay to include virtual as well as physical networks.

Corrected packet capture, network TAP, signature detection, honeypot and base-rate definitions that had absolute coverage/accuracy claims. Recording bytes at 1 Gbps is distinguished from a physical link rate. IPFIX flow templates are not universally payload-free.
Distinguished generic flow logs from the AWS product; AWS REJECT includes packets after closure, Nitro aggregation overrides the default, and sampling/coverage/delivery delay remain explicit.

Narrowed broad aliases such as association, entropy, URI-as-URL, generic flow logs-as-AWS, source validation-as-BCP38 and disassociation-as-deauthentication. Added four precise missing entries: rogue AP, URI, Transition Disable and generic flow log.

Added explanatory comments to all seven Python fences without altering executable ASTs. Labels distinguish real Suricata, nftables, shell and configuration syntax from drawings. Added explicit arithmetic grouping and conventional implicit algebra in lesson and question cards.

corrections: nsec-dos-resources: Cloudflare 29.7 Tbps (2025 Q3 report) was no longer Cloudflare's largest reported attack -> record 31.4 Tbps, about 35 seconds, from the 2025 Q4 report (5 Feb 2026), dated "as of October 2026" after checking the H1 2026 and 2026 Q3 reports; link updated.

nsec-amplification-budget: "reflected through DNS resolvers with a BAF of about 50" contradicted the table's 28.7 for open resolvers (inherited from baseline) -> "DNS servers with a BAF of about 50 (a round figure near the table's authoritative-server measurement)".
nsec-tls-handshake-proof: added RFC 9846 s4.1.3's limit on the DOWNGRD sentinel: it protects only when the TLS 1.2 handshake signs the server random (ephemeral key exchange), not with static RSA.

nsec-vpns-q9 workedExample: "some gateways fragment ... others drop it and rely on an ICMP message reaching the sender" -> RFC 4301 s8 behaviour: the outer DF bit is set, cleared or copied per SA; with DF clear the outer packet is fragmented, with DF set the ICMP must reach the gateway so it can lower the SA path MTU and signal the inner senders.
nsec-vpns-q9 option 3 explanation: presented ESP padding as always 0-3 bytes for 4-byte alignment -> depends on the cipher's alignment and packet length (0-3 bytes for AES-GCM).
nsec-wireless-q9 workedExample: stale "lesson 1's MITM principle" -> "the man-in-the-middle principle from the threat units".

nsec-krack-key-state: the fact wireless-q6 needs (KRACK does not recover the passphrase or PMK) existed only inside the collapsed analogy -> visible sentence sourced from krackattacks.com, including that changing the password does not help.
nsec-wpa2-derived-keys: the key fact that every WPA2-Personal passphrase holder derives the same PMK (and can derive a captured client's PTK) existed only in the analogy limit -> visible sentence.
nsec-alert-base-rates reference formula: "tp / (tp + f(1 − p))" read as a function call -> "tp / (tp + (1 − p)f)".

Wrong-sense links: "MAC-table exhaustion" (bare MAC -> medium access control) -> "exhausting the switch's MAC address table" (nsec-packet-identities); takeaway "Segment remote users" (verb -> TCP segment) -> "Put remote users in their own network segment" (nsec-vpn-access-boundaries).

lowConfidence.claim: Cloudflare's record 31.4 Tbps attack (2025 Q4 report, Feb 2026) is still the largest it has reported as of October 2026.
lowConfidence.reason: Provider-reported measurement; the "still largest" part rests on the H1 2026 and 2026 Q3 reports (fetched 2026-10-30) not reporting a larger one, and a new record can be announced at any time. Dated and attributed in the text.

lowConfidence.claim: Maximum validity 398/200/100/47 days by issue date (15 Mar 2026, 15 Mar 2027, 15 Mar 2029).
lowConfidence.reason: Verified in BR v2.3.1 (4 Oct 2026) s6.3.2, but CA/Browser Forum ballots can change the schedule; the lesson dates and hedges it.

lowConfidence.claim: Let's Encrypt turned off OCSP in August 2025 and publishes revocation only via CRLs; BR SC063 made OCSP optional from March 2024.
lowConfidence.reason: Verified in the Let's Encrypt post (6 Aug 2025) and the BR revision table; provider policy can change.

lowConfidence.claim: vpns-q9: after moving behind NAT, full-size packets exceed the link by 8 bytes and stall when ICMP is blocked.
lowConfidence.reason: NAT-T overhead and RFC 4301 DF handling verified; actual behaviour depends on the gateway's DF-bit policy and where the 1,500-byte limit sits, which the worked example now states.

lowConfidence.claim: Most web traffic is encrypted and encrypted bytes barely compress; teams commonly keep summaries longer than full packets.
lowConfidence.reason: General practice statements, hedged in the text; no single measurement cited.

nsec-packet-filter-reading.rationale: No formula; tcpdump/Wireshark syntax and flag reading are procedures. Only the reading list changed. q2/q3/q5 unchanged.

nsec-capture-offloads-storage.rationale: Storage formula removed (routine unit conversion); prose figures recomputed: 1 Gbps = 125 MB/s = 10.8 TB/day, 324 TB/30 days, 648 TB at 2 Gbps ("about 650"). detection-q8 (100 TB holds 4.6 days at 21.6 TB/day) and q9 (1,500 - 20 - 32 = 1,448; 28,960 / 1,448 = 20) recomputed.

questionsRewritten.nsec-detection-q8: (claude-opus-5-5/cf2-net-sec-author2) Was a 2 Gbps x 30 days storage calculation; now a retention-planning decision under a 100 TB budget, with the data in the prompt. Numbers recomputed.
questionsRewritten.nsec-detection-q9: (claude-opus-5-5/cf2-net-sec-author2) Worked example only: formula card replaced by two prose steps (1,448-byte segments; exactly 20 of them).

nsec-encrypted-traffic-evidence.rationale: No formula; metadata signals and their limits unchanged; reading list now includes RFC 9849. q6 unchanged.

nsec-flow-record-investigations.rationale: No formula. Scan-detector Python executed (prints "10.0.2.7 1 0 " and "203.0.113.9 5 4 SCAN?"), matching the text and q11. VPC Flow Logs facts are baseline. q10/q11 unchanged.

author.note: cf2-net-sec-author made the concept-first edits, analogies and question rewrites for the first 30 lessons (nsec-packet-identities to nsec-enterprise-wifi-identities) and stopped without a report; cf2-net-sec-author2 re-checked that work, edited the six detection lessons, improved the NXDOMAIN glossary entry, ran the code and wrote the frozen report (evidence/cf2-net-sec-author2.json), 2026-10-30.

nsec-packet-identities.rationale: Forged sender name on a letter: maps the unauthenticated source field and replies going to the forged address; limit names BCP 38 filtering and TCP/TLS state, which the post has no equivalent of (RFC 2827 fetched). Kept: a familiar, accurate picture of why spoofing suits one-way attacks.

nsec-authentication-replay.rationale: Numbered cheques: signature = message authentication, cheque number = nonce/sequence number, record of paid numbers = receiver replay state, stale-cheque rule = timestamp window. Limit (bit-identical copies, atomic check) is accurate. Kept as the module's single replay analogy; the IPsec replay-window cloakroom analogy that repeated it was removed.

nsec-dos-resources.rationale: Three ways to stop a restaurant (road, booked tables, kitchen) map bandwidth, retained state and application work, and the SYN-cookie "hold no table until the guest confirms" mapping is fair. Limit (mixed/spoofed attacks, anycast) accurate. Kept: it organises the lesson's three-way classification.

nsec-amplification-budget.rationale: Free catalogues mailed to a victim's address: postcard = spoofed request, firms = reflectors, catalogue weight ratio = BAF. Limit (reflector capacity, BCP 38) accurate. Kept as the module's reflection analogy; the follow-on parcel analogy in the next unit was removed as a repeat.

nsec-amplification-controls.rationale: Removed by the verifier: the "shop that only posts parcels to verified addresses" repeated the previous unit's mail-order catalogue scenario, and the QUIC three-times rule it illustrated is already a plain, visible rule in the paragraph above it. No question depended on it.

nsec-firewall-rule-order.rationale: Door supervisor's ordered checklist: lines = rules, first fitting line = first match, unmentioned guests refused = default deny, broad line above narrow = shadowing. Limit (no judgement; AWS security groups unordered; nftables chains) accurate. Kept: it makes shadowing concrete.

nsec-firewall-state-cloud.rationale: Receptionist's log of expected replies maps the connection table and stateless broad return rules; limit (memory, expiry, no sender proof) is the important caveat. Kept: it clarifies why NACLs need ephemeral-port rules.

nsec-segmentation-boundaries.rationale: Fire doors and compartments map segments, internal policy points and lateral movement/blast radius; the limit (an attacker chooses permitted paths; monitoring needed) prevents the misleading "segmentation stops attackers" reading. Kept.

nsec-zero-trust-access.rationale: Keycards checked at every ward door: per-resource decisions, central revocation and logging versus front-desk perimeter trust. Limit (device posture, software policy, segmentation remains) accurate. Kept as the module's single access-control-by-door analogy; the VPN "key to every door" and mTLS "badges" analogies that repeated it were removed.

nsec-tls-security-properties.rationale: Removed by the verifier: the signet-ring/shredded-combination scene combined two unrelated props and its main mapping (agreeing a combination in front of an observer) needed a limit that undid it; the visible forward-secrecy paragraph already explains the mechanism concretely.

nsec-tls-handshake-proof.rationale: Signed minutes of a meeting carried by a courier: the minutes are the transcript, signatures/keyed MACs are CertificateVerify and Finished, a meddling courier is a downgrade attempt. Limit (no protection against non-delivery or client fallback) accurate. Kept: transcript binding is abstract and this is its clearest familiar picture.

nsec-tls-resumption-replay.rationale: Replay is already given an analogy (numbered cheques) in nsec-authentication-replay, and this lesson uses a concrete catalogue-versus-charge example; a second comparison would repeat it.

nsec-tls-certificate-path.rationale: Passport at a border: issuing office = intermediate CA, government list = trust store, photo/name = SAN match, document type and expiry = EKU/validity. Limit (signatures, CertificateVerify proof of key, differing trust stores) accurate. Kept.

nsec-tls-certificate-operations.rationale: Cancelled bank cards and short expiry: printed hot list = CRL, phoning the bank = OCSP (including the privacy leak Let's Encrypt cites), accepting when the line is down = soft-fail, short expiry = short-lived certificates. Limit (automation, misuse before expiry) accurate. Kept: it explains soft-fail, which the prose states only briefly.

nsec-tls-ech-privacy.rationale: Sealed letter inside a mailroom envelope: outer envelope = outer ClientHello with public name, inner = encrypted inner ClientHello, tower of companies = anonymity set. Limit (single-tenant building, plaintext DNS) maps the lesson's real caveats. Kept.

nsec-tls-mutual-authentication.rationale: Removed by the verifier: the "two staff badges" analogy needed a door that "displays its own sign" for server authentication and a phoning receptionist for load-balancer termination, a forced multi-part mapping that repeated the zero-trust keycard picture. The visible bullets already state authn vs authz and the termination trust boundary.

nsec-tunnel-byte-budgets.rationale: Removed by the verifier: the padded-mailer analogy restated a one-line subtraction already shown by the ASCII diagram and formula, and immediately preceded the next unit's low-bridge size analogy, so it added repetition rather than understanding.

nsec-tunnel-pmtu.rationale: Low bridge with no warning sign: bridge height = reduced path MTU, tall lorries = full-size DF packets, removed sign = blocked ICMP Packet Too Big, loading lower vehicles = MSS clamp. Limit (retransmission, UDP not fixed by MSS clamping) accurate. Kept: it makes the black-hole symptom memorable.

nsec-ipsec-security-associations.rationale: Courier contract then sealed pouches: meeting = IKEv2 control plane, pouches = ESP, reference number = SPI, one agreement per direction = unidirectional SAs. Limit (IKE keeps running; UDP 4500 blocked leaves a negotiated but empty tunnel) matches vpns-q6. Kept: it separates the two planes clearly.

nsec-ipsec-replay-window.rationale: Removed by the verifier: the cloakroom-ticket analogy was forced (cloakrooms do not refuse old unused tickets) and repeated the numbered-cheque replay analogy in nsec-authentication-replay; the executed trace and table teach the window directly.

nsec-wireguard-peer-routing.rationale: Couriers with named delivery rounds: seal = public key, district list = AllowedIPs, most precise list = longest-prefix match, reception check = inbound source test. Limit (OS routing first, no negotiation) accurate. Kept: cryptokey routing is otherwise abstract.

nsec-vxlan-isolation.rationale: Removed by the verifier: the painted-crate analogy restated the visible "VXLAN has no security" warning that immediately follows it (a VNI is a label, not a credential) and added no new understanding.

nsec-vpn-access-boundaries.rationale: Removed by the verifier: "a key to every door for one job" repeated the zero-trust keycard building analogy in nsec-zero-trust-access; the lesson's own concrete dashboard example already makes the least-privilege point.

nsec-wifi-wep-reused-ivs.rationale: One-time pad used twice is the standard "two-time pad" picture of keystream reuse; the crib ("Dear Sir") point adds the idea that predictable plaintext unravels the XOR. Limit (RC4 key recovery is a further flaw) accurate. Kept.

nsec-wep-keying-integrity.rationale: Shop-bought tamper sticker versus a signet seal maps unkeyed CRC versus a keyed MAC; limit (blind bit-flipping without reading) is the technically important difference. Kept.

nsec-wpa2-derived-keys.rationale: Removed by the verifier: the hotel master-code analogy was forced (how hotels cut key cards is not familiar) and its stated limit contradicted the central property it was meant to illustrate (in WPA2-Personal every passphrase holder knows the PMK). That property is now visible prose.

nsec-wpa2-offline-guesses.rationale: A copy of the lock taken home is the standard offline-versus-online guessing picture: no lockout, speed limited only by the attacker's resources. Limit (handshake contains a test, not the passphrase; SAE gives no such copy) accurate. Kept.

nsec-krack-key-state.rationale: Removed by the verifier: the reset receipt-counter analogy was forced (receipt numbers tied to a "day's code" are not a familiar mechanism) and its only extra fact (no passphrase recovery) was question-critical, so that fact now sits in the visible text.

nsec-wpa3-sae-transition.rationale: New front door with the old back door still open on the same code maps transition mode and the shared passphrase; limit (transition disable, online guessing) accurate. Kept: the weakest accepted option setting the security level is the key idea.

nsec-enterprise-wifi-identities.rationale: Personal staff passes instead of one door code maps per-user revocation and logging; the fake guard maps an evil-twin RADIUS server and checking credentials maps CA/name validation. Limit (cryptographic check, shared GTK) accurate. Kept: it is the clearest picture of why 802.1X beats a shared PSK.

nsec-ids-placement-signatures.rationale: CCTV room versus a door supervisor maps passive copy versus inline blocking, fail-open/closed and false-positive blocks; limit (mirror loss, encryption, automated responses) accurate. Kept.

nsec-alert-base-rates.rationale: Screening a population for a rare illness is the canonical base-rate illustration (1 in 10,000 prevalence with a 1-in-1,000 false-positive rate gives about ten false alarms per real case). Limit (adaptive attackers, non-independent events) accurate. Kept.

nsec-packet-filter-reading.rationale: Tool syntax and flag interpretation are procedures; an analogy would not add understanding.

nsec-capture-offloads-storage.rationale: Offload artefacts and storage scaling are concrete operational facts; the detail-versus-cost idea already has the itemised phone-bill analogy in nsec-flow-record-investigations.

nsec-encrypted-traffic-evidence.rationale: The visible-outside/hidden-inside idea already has the sealed-letter analogy in nsec-tls-ech-privacy; repeating it would add little.

nsec-flow-record-investigations.rationale: Itemised phone bill versus a call recording maps flow records versus packet capture; limit (sampling, split records, aggregation windows, Amazon DNS gap) is accurate and lesson-specific. Kept.
